# Working Report — ADR-0107, the provenance of the documentation prose

This document reports the work that wrote one decision record. It is a record
of one moment, and nobody maintains it.

Date of the work: 3 September 2026.

## 1. The scope test, applied to two candidate claims

The record scope rule gives three conditions. A decision needs a record only
when all three hold.[^1] The work applied the test twice, in writing, before it
wrote anything.

### 1.1 Candidate A: the provenance of the documentation prose

**The claim.** The published Python reference is generated by an import of the
compiled extension module, and the prose of a member that module provides lives
in the Rust doc comment and never in the type stub.

**Condition 1, a future contributor could reasonably choose otherwise. It
holds, and more strongly than the dispatcher stated.** The stub exists, it
already carries prose for some members, and the documentation handler's own
guide recommends turning module inspection off when a stub exists.[^2] So a
contributor who chooses otherwise is not careless. That contributor is
following the tool's advice. The build then succeeds, reports nothing, and
publishes a reference with signatures and no prose. The research report
measured that fall.[^2]

**Condition 2, a different choice costs more than a change made later. It
holds.** The wrong choice moves the whole of the bindings crate's prose into a
second file. Unwinding it means deciding, for every member, which of two copies
is authoritative, and no check exists to tell a reader which one drifted. The
cost is not the copy. The cost is that the two sites are then both plausible.

**Condition 3, the reasoning is not visible in the artefact. It holds.** A
configuration file that disables inspection looks correct. A stub with a
docstring on every method looks better maintained than one without. Neither
artefact says why the project refuses them, and the failure they cause is a
smaller page rather than an error.

**Verdict: the claim passes all three conditions.** The record was written.

The dispatcher's reasoning was checked rather than accepted, and it holds on
all three conditions. One part of it was understated: the record's own evidence
shows the wrong choice is already partly made. The stub carries eleven
docstrings that copy the Rust source today.

### 1.2 Candidate B: the project uses Zensical to build the documentation

**Condition 1 holds.** Three other builders are real candidates and the report
examined all three.[^2]

**Condition 2 fails.** The site configuration is a portable format that a second
builder reads without change, and the report treats the swap as one command.
A record buys the right to refuse a change, and this change costs almost
nothing to make later. A record here would add friction and buy nothing.

**Condition 3 is arguable and does not matter.** The reason for the choice is
not visible in a manifest that names a tool. The test needs all three
conditions, and the second one already failed.

**Verdict: the claim fails the test.** The dispatcher's judgement was correct.
The record names the builder once, in the consequences, as the tool the project
uses now. The record scope rule also forbids the release pin that a body
mention of a young tool invites.[^1]

### 1.3 A third candidate, considered and left out

**The claim.** The site configuration stays in a format that more than one
builder reads.

This one is close to the line. It passes condition 1, it arguably passes
condition 3, and condition 2 is the interesting one: the configuration file is
cheap to rewrite, but the escape hatch is the whole reason the project can adopt
a young builder honestly.

**It was left out because it is a second claim, and it can be accepted
separately.** The scope rule says to split a record that states two claims that
a reviewer could accept on their own.[^1] A record about where prose lives and a
record about how a build stays portable are two records. The choice therefore
went to the decisions register as an open row, rather than into this record as a
fifth decision.[^3]

## 2. What the record binds

Four decisions, one claim.

- **D1.** The published Python reference is generated by an import of the
  compiled extension module.
- **D2.** The prose of a member the compiled module provides lives in the Rust
  doc comment of the bindings crate, and nowhere else.
- **D3.** The type stub declares types. It carries prose only for a declaration
  the compiled module does not provide, such as a typed dictionary that
  describes a returned mapping.
- **D4.** The documentation job builds the extension before it builds the site,
  and it fails when the import fails.

D4 is the decision that makes D1 enforceable. Without it, a build that falls
back to the stub publishes a smaller page and reports nothing, so the guard
would depend on a reader noticing.

## 3. What was deliberately left out of the body, and why

**Every measured figure.** The page sizes, the build times, the footnote counts
and the heading counts stay in the research report.[^2] The scope rule forbids a
measured figure in a record body, because a better measurement arrives more
often than a decision changes.[^1]

**Every version and release.** No version of any tool appears in the record. The
report holds them, with the date the author read each one.

**The alpha status of the builder.** The dispatcher asked for this and it is
also the correct reading of the rule: a development status is a property of a
release, and a release changes. The record states the durable form instead. The
builder is replaceable, the constraints hold whichever builder runs, and a
change of builder is not a change to the record.

**Every count.** The record names "nine exception docstrings and one class
docstring" in one consequence, and that is a count. It is kept on purpose,
because it names a defect the record refuses to fix rather than a property of
the tree, and the finding and the backlog item both carry the same figure. It
is the one place the record comes close to the rule against counts, and a
reviewer may reasonably ask for it to go.

**The module arrangement.** The record names no directory, no file layout and no
navigation. It names the crate boundary once, which the scope rule permits as
the legitimate exception, because a compiler enforces that boundary.[^1]

**The documentation itself.** No page, no site, no navigation, no workflow, and
no dependency was added. Those are separate items under the same record.

## 4. The repair to the package docstring

**What was wrong.** The top-level docstring of the Python package said the
package is a stub, and that the selector interface, the verb interface and the
view scope are not written yet. The selector interface is not written. The other
two are. A finding records it and deliberately left the repair to this work.[^4]

**What the repair does.** It removes the sentence, and it does not replace it
with a corrected list.

A corrected list would be a second place that states what the package holds,
which is the defect shape the finding names and the reason the previous worker
declined to fix the sentence alone.[^5] The new docstring says instead that it
does not list what the package holds, says why, names the case that already went
wrong, and cites the record that puts the answer in the generated reference.
It keeps the boundary rule and the statement that nothing enforces it, because
neither of those is a list of contents.

**The repair is consistent with the record.** The package entry point is pure
Python, so its docstring is not a member the compiled module provides, and D3
does not reach it. What the record does is remove the reason to write the list:
the reference reports what the module holds, so a hand-written summary buys
nothing and decays.

## 5. The decision about the stub docstring

**The false claim was repaired here. The generator was not written, and a
backlog item holds it.**

The stub docstring claimed that the build regenerates the stub and that a job
fails on a difference. No generator and no such job exists.[^6]

**The repair belongs to this work, for two reasons.** The first is that a false
statement about a check is worse than no statement: a contributor who reads it
concludes that something protects the second declaration site. The second is
that this record is the record that governs the file. It states what the stub is
for, so leaving the file describing itself falsely would put the record and the
artefact in disagreement on the day the record was written.

**The generator does not belong to this work.** It is a build change with two
checks and a removal of eleven docstrings. Backlog item 0307 holds it, and it
sits in the `Next` group of the backlog priority index beside the two other
items about one fact in two places.[^7]

The new stub docstring states plainly that no generator and no check exists, so
the file now describes itself correctly and names the item that changes it.

## 6. The finding

**FND-321.** The register already recorded that the stub and the compiled module
are two declaration sites that disagree.[^6] The disagreement it named is an
absence: no method of the two main classes carries a docstring in the stub.

This work found the sharper half. The stub carries eleven docstrings that copy
the Rust source. Nine exception docstrings agree with the Rust strings character
for character. One class docstring is a one line copy that agrees. One class
docstring is an abridged copy that does not agree, and the paragraph it dropped
is the paragraph that warns against one value in two places with nothing failing
when the copies disagree.

An agreeing copy is the worse case. It reads as a maintained file, so nothing
prompts a contributor to look for the other site.

## 7. The registers

- **Registry.** The row for 0107 was added with status `Draft` and the
  dependencies before the file was written. The author set `Draft` and nothing
  beyond it.[^8]
- **Decision record priority index.** 0107 is in the "Waiting for review" table,
  below 0106. It says what a reviewer should test hardest and that the author
  must not review it.[^9]
- **Decisions register.** DEC-112 is closed with the outcome and the reasoning.
  DEC-113 is open, and it holds the configuration format question that section
  1.3 declined to bind.[^3]
- **Findings register.** FND-321 was added.[^10]
- **Backlog.** Item 0307 was added to `proposed/` and placed in the priority
  index.[^7]
- **Blockers.** None was opened and none was closed. Nothing here waits on
  missing information. The blocker number the dispatcher reserved is unused.

**Two reserved numbers are unused.** The dispatcher reserved two findings
numbers and one blocker number. This work took the first findings number and
needed neither of the other two. The register check derives the next findings
number from the highest entry, so a deliberate gap was rejected and the
next-number line now points at the second reserved number. A later writer will
take it, which is safe, because a number is never reused.

## 8. The gates

    just records          0 failures across eight checks, 2 pre-existing notes
    just records-probe    0 failures
    just merge-defects    0 failures
    just lint-python      ruff clean, mypy clean over 18 source files
    just test-python      74 passed

The two notes from the record check name two records that nothing cites. Both
predate this work.

**Two check failures were found and fixed during the run, and both are worth
naming.** The register check derives the next findings number from the highest
entry, so the deliberate gap this work left in the numbering was rejected. The
footnote check refused a second label for a source another footnote already
names in the same document.

**The Rust gates were not run.** This change touches no Rust source. Formatting,
lint, the test suite and the two determinism tests were not exercised. That is a
skipped step and not a green claim.

## 9. What was left undone

- **No documentation build exists.** No site, no navigation, no page, no
  workflow and no dependency was added. That was out of scope.
- **Nothing enforces D2 or D3.** The record states the constraint and no check
  reads it. Backlog item 0307 is the enforcement, and it is unrefined.
- **The eleven copied docstrings are still in the stub.** The stub now says so
  and names the item that removes them.
- **The record is a draft and binds nothing.** Only a reviewer may accept it,
  and the author must not be that reviewer.
